To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed the first quantitative model of DNA separation in a microfluidic device using viscoelastic liquids and that the model is capable of predicting device separation performance with a single adjustable parameter.
a quantitative model of the DNA separation in the μLAS microfluidic device is proposed.

a simple model of DNA transport in the μLAS technology, based on hydrodynamics first-principles and statistical mechanics, is able to quantitatively describe DNA transport in a microfluidic channel, and that this model can be used for the design of DNA size-separation devices with a resolution of 7 bp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of microfluidic technologies to separate, concentrate, and analyze DNA.
the development of a new class of microfluidic devices, μLaser-Actuated Systems (μLAS), that enable the separation, concentration and analysis of DNA with high sensitivity.
the development of microfluidic technologies for DNA separation, analysis, and detection, and the development of a model for the prediction of device performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new DNA separation technology that is capable of achieving high resolution separations and that is based on the use of a viscoelastic liquid as the separation medium.
the present study provides a new and powerful tool for the design and optimization of microfluidic devices for DNA separation and concentration.
our work provides the first quantitative model that describes the DNA transport in the μLAS device.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a quantitative model is developed for the transport of charged macromolecules in microchannels with viscoelastic liquids under the action of electrohydrodynamic flow actuation.
we developed a model to describe DNA separation in viscoelastic solutions and used this model to predict the resolution length of our device.
we have developed a model for DNA separation in viscoelastic solutions that is in agreement with experiments, and that we have identified conditions to achieve maximal resolution lengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of hydrodynamics and statistical mechanics can provide a quantitative model for the transport of DNA in microfluidic systems.

the μLAS technology can be used to separate and concentrate DNA molecules with a resolution that is not limited by the diffusion of DNA molecules, and that the resolution is only limited by the size of the DNA fragments.
DNA separation in μLAS is not a purely diffusive process, but rather a combination of diffusion and viscoelastic transport, which is the key to its high performance.
